decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach to the left tube; keep right arm parked. Geometry will be refined from closer views.
Continue with reduced increments after continuity rejection; move inward above the left tube while pitching toward a top grasp.
Align the left gripper over the tube body, with fingers across its axis; approach to a hover before closing.
Refine left grasp toward the tube's upper body using wrist view, lower slightly, and close fully.
Lift the closed left gripper and tube clear of the table, retaining the grasp before reorienting upright.
Tube remains between the fingers. Rotate it toward upright above the left rack area with a closed gripper and small continuous wrist motion.
Finish rotating the held tube upright and bring it above a left-side large rack opening.
Reduce wrist increments after the guard interruption; finish upright alignment over the left large slot.
Lower the upright tube toward the front-left large opening, with a small visual alignment correction; keep the grasp closed.
Seat the left tube slowly to rack depth while maintaining upright orientation; inspect alignment before release.
Tube appears to have contacted the slot rim. Relieve contact, shift a few millimeters toward the visible opening center, and reseat slowly.
Release the aligned tube over the opening and withdraw slightly, checking whether it settles upright in the rack.
First tube is visibly seated and released. Withdraw the left arm and start the right elbow-up approach to the nearer right tube.
Return the empty left arm toward home while aligning the right gripper across the nearer tube's diagonal axis.
Finish right-arm orientation and approach to a short hover above the nearer tube. Bring the empty left arm to its home vicinity.
Refine the right gripper to the tube's upper body, descend the final few centimeters, then close for a retention test.
Lift the second tube clear with the right gripper fully closed, checking retention before rotating toward the rack.
The second tube is retained. Begin a gradual upright rotation while moving toward a right-side rack slot.
Continue the smooth right-arm reorientation and carry the retained tube closer above the right rack opening.
Finish upright orientation above the rightmost large slot using small continuous increments.
Lower the retained upright second tube toward the rightmost opening, then inspect the slot alignment before final seating.
Slowly seat the second tube into the right-side large opening, keeping it upright and the gripper closed for inspection.
Open the right gripper to release the seated second tube, then back away slightly to verify that it remains upright in the slot.
Both released tubes appear seated. Raise the empty right gripper clear of the rack before approaching the remaining rear-right tube.
Reorient the empty right gripper toward a top grasp and advance toward the remaining tube, keeping clearance above the rack.
Continue the right-arm approach above the remaining tube, rotating the open gripper toward its diagonal axis.
Finish aligning the right gripper above the remaining rear tube, adapting wrist yaw to its diagonal direction before descending.
Use the wrist view to center the remaining tube between the fingers, correct its diagonal alignment, and descend to grasp height.
Make the final small upper-body grasp adjustment on the third tube, then close the right gripper fully.
Lift the third tube clear while keeping the right gripper closed; verify retention before carrying it to the remaining rack opening.
Third tube is retained. Rotate it gradually upright while carrying it toward the empty central rack opening, keeping the right arm on its side.
Continue upright reorientation and inward transport above the empty central slot, with the tube securely between closed fingers.
Finish upright alignment of the third tube above the central large opening, using small continuous right-arm movements.
Lower the upright third tube toward the central slot with the right gripper closed, maintaining clearance from the two inserted tubes.
Seat the third tube slowly into the central opening while preserving its upright alignment and closed grasp.
The third tube appears to have met the rim rather than fully seated. Relieve contact, shift slightly toward the opening center, and reseat gently.
Release the third tube over the aligned central opening and withdraw a little, checking that it settles to the same depth as the others.
The third tube tilted instead of seating. Attempt a careful regrasp of its lower body and a short lift, avoiding the two seated tubes.
The recovery grasp was empty; the third tube now lies across the rack. Open and lift clear to approach it from above without disturbing the seated tubes.
Approach the fallen tube's right-hand end from above with the open right gripper; keep the arm on its side and the other tubes clear.
Continue the overhead recovery approach to the tube's exposed right end, with small joint-continuous movements and open fingers.
Finish turning the right gripper downward above the fallen tube's exposed end; descend only to a hover before refining the grasp.
After the continuity interruption, use smaller rotations and lower the hover while moving toward the exposed tube end, keeping the right EE on its side.
Change to a tilted overhead approach rather than extending farther: retract slightly and angle the open fingers toward the fallen tube while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Center the exposed tube body in the tilted overhead gripper with a small wrist-guided adjustment, then close gently for recovery.
Complete closure around the exposed tube body, then test retention with a short vertical lift away from the rack.
The tube did not follow the lift. Open and withdraw the right arm; approach its left-side body with the left arm instead, keeping the arms separated.
Continue a tilted left-arm approach toward the fallen tube's cap-side body while moving the empty right arm back toward its own home workspace.
Advance the left open gripper above the fallen tube's left half while continuing to park the right arm clear of the rack.
Bring the tilted left gripper above the fallen tube's cap-side body, aligning its fingers across the tube. Continue returning the right arm home.
With smaller return increments after the guard stop, park the right arm. Shift the left fingers onto the fallen tube body and descend carefully above the rack.
Unexpected contact prevented the left approach. Open and lift clear rather than pushing, then reassess the tube and rack alignment.
